title: SSE models
text:
Skip to main content
In this tutorial you fit BiSSE, a state-dependent speciation and extinction model, to habitat_binary. You read its diagnostics, then try the MuSSE, QuaSSE and hidden-state cards. The small example is for learning the controls and the checks, not for testing a hypothesis.

title: SSE models
text:
Before you start
Open SSE models, then its Data card. Load the example and click Use matched taxa. Resolve the mismatch shows each step.

title: SSE models
text:
BiSSE
BiSSE fits separate speciation (λ₀, λ₁) and extinction (μ₀, μ₁) rates for two observed states, plus transition rates between them.


Open the BiSSE card.
Set Binary trait to habitat_binary.
Choose the Observed value coded as state 0. The other value becomes state 1.
Under Models, keep the defaults: Full and Trait-independent diversification.
Click Run BiSSE.
Open Diagnostics before you look at Results.





BiSSE diagnostics open with warnings, verification status and every optimizer start.



Read the diagnostics
With the synthetic example, expect Diagnostics to open with warnings, including “A BiSSE rate reached a bound”. This is the app doing its job. Check these points before you trust any estimate:

Bounds. A rate at its bound is not a reliable estimate. Look at which parameter hit the bound in Effective parameter constraints.
Optimizer starts. Compare the log-likelihoods across starts. If starts disagree, refit before you interpret the result.
Independent verification. Check that each model was verified by an independent optimizer.
Data size. Few taxa or an unbalanced trait give weakly identified rates. A 19-tip example is small.



Profile uncertainty
After a fit, you can profile one rate:


In Graph controls, choose the Model and Parameter to profile.
In Analysis controls, open Profile uncertainty. Enter finite Profile lower search bound and Profile upper search bound values that enclose the estimate.
Click Run profile uncertainty.
Read the interval and profile grid in Diagnostics. An unresolved endpoint is shown as unavailable.

title: SSE models
text:
MuSSE
MuSSE extends BiSSE to 2 to 8 observed categorical states.


Open the MuSSE card.
Set Discrete trait to locomotion_3state.
Click Fill state table and check the state-to-code mapping.
Click Run MuSSE.


The number of parameters grows quickly with the number of states. For the state table format, see Custom input formats.

title: SSE models
text:
QuaSSE
QuaSSE links speciation and extinction to a continuous trait.


Open the QuaSSE card.
Set Continuous trait to body_mass.
For practice, enter 10 in Common measurement standard error. This is an invented value, not a biological measurement.
Click Run QuaSSE.
Click Run grid and domain refits as an extra numerical check.


Check grid resolution, integration stability and optimizer verification in Diagnostics. With real data, you must justify any measurement error you supply.

title: SSE models
text:
Hidden-state and null models
This card compares hidden-state models (HiSSE) with character-independent null models (CID-2, CID-4). Hidden classes are latent rate categories, not observed traits.


Open the Hidden-state and null models card.
Set Binary trait to habitat_binary and choose State 0.
Under Models, keep HiSSE, CID-2 and CID-4.
Click Run hidden-state models.
In Diagnostics, check native termination and independent verification before you use any comparison.

title: SSE models
text:
Why weights may be withheld
Guane may show a finite likelihood but no model weight. It withholds weights unless the fits pass checks for convergence, repeatability, bounds and independent verification. The warnings in Diagnostics explain which check failed.
Compare AIC only within one card run. Do not compare AIC between the BiSSE, MuSSE, QuaSSE and hidden-state cards.

title: SSE models
text:
Before you interpret






Scientific caution




A BiSSE preference for trait-dependent rates can be produced by rate differences unrelated to the trait. Refit in Hidden-state and null models and compare against CID-2 and CID-4 before you interpret it.
A trait-dependent rate is an association under the model, not proof that the trait caused diversification.
Rates at bounds, disagreeing starts or failed verification mean the estimate is not reliable.
Multistate hidden-state models, calibrated SSE tests and QuaSSE or hidden-state intervals are not available.

Read State-dependent speciation and extinction before you report.

title: Diversification
text:
Skip to main content
In this tutorial you plot lineages through time (LTT) for the example tree. You then fit constant-rate models and see where the other rate cards fit. Diversification cards use the tree only.

title: Diversification
text:
Before you start
Open Diversification, then its Data card, and click Load example data. These cards use the tree only, so you do not need to match taxa. See Example data and the Data card for what the example contains.

title: Diversification
text:
Lineage through time
An LTT curve counts the surviving lineages in a tree through its history. It is a description of the tree. It does not estimate speciation or extinction.


Open the Lineage through time card.
Leave Tree source set to Data tree.
Click Run LTT.
In Graph controls, change Time direction from Since origin to Before present, or tick Logarithmic lineage axis.





The LTT curve for the example tree. The time axis is in branch-length units.


To overlay several trees, set Tree source to Uploaded tree set and upload up to 25 Newick files. Only overlay trees with comparable sampling and branch-length units.

title: Diversification
text:
Constant-rate models


Open the Constant-rate models card.
Under Models, keep both Yule (mu = 0) and Birth-death selected.
Click Run diversification models.
In Results, Graph starts at Rate estimates. Set it to Model comparison to see ΔAIC for each model.
Click Run uncertainty and diagnostics for profile likelihoods and conditional LTT checks.





The model comparison graph shows ΔAIC bars for the two fits.


With the synthetic example, expect the app to say the data do not clearly distinguish the selected models. That is the honest reading: a 20-tip tree carries little information about extinction.

title: Diversification
text:
Other rate cards
Each remaining card answers a different rate question. Run each one the same way: set its options, click its run button, then read Results and Diagnostics.









Card
First run with the example
How to read it




Time-varying models
Keep the default candidates (Yule, BD, ExpYule, ExpBD). Click Run time-varying comparison.
View rates through time. Run time-model uncertainty adds profile, bootstrap and robustness checks. An exponential curve is a model assumption.


Clade-specific models
Choose non-overlapping Crown nodes with at least four tips each. Click Preview selected clades, then Run clade models.
Each clade is fitted separately. Compare models within a clade, not AIC across clades.


Joint clade-dependent models
Choose Joint shift nodes. Click Preview joint regions, then Run joint models.
One whole-tree likelihood with shared or shifted rates. Shifts sit at the base of the chosen branch.


Diversity-dependent models
Keep the default model. Click Run diversity-dependent models, then Run numerical diagnostics.
Curves relate rates to modeled diversity. Run uncertainty and robustness adds optional checks with more assumptions.




For every rate card, check failed starts, parameter bounds and numerical stability before you read estimates or model weights. Sampling fractions are taken as given. For clade and region sampling tables, see Custom input formats.

title: Diversification
text:
Before you interpret






Scientific caution




Rates are per branch-length unit. The example tree is not dated.
An LTT curve describes the tree; it does not estimate speciation or extinction.
Extinction estimates from a small tree of living species are very sensitive to assumptions.

Read LTT and whole tree diversification, Clade dependent diversification and Diversity dependent diversification before you report.

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
Sampling and root


Sampling fraction for state 0
The share of living species in state 0 that your tree includes. Sampling fraction for state 1 does the same for state 1.

Where

BiSSE Model and data settings

Default

1 for each state

Change it when

Species in one state are better sampled than in the other. Unequal sampling can mimic state-dependent diversification.

Check after

The model line in Results shows sampling.f.




Root treatment
Sets how the root state is weighted in the likelihood.

Where

BiSSE Model and data settings Root treatment

Default

Observed (ROOT.OBS)

Change it when

You have a justified root prior. Given (ROOT.GIVEN) opens Root probability for state 0.

Check after

The model line in Results shows root. Every candidate in the run uses the same root treatment.

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
Constraints and search

BiSSE parameter table (CSV)
Ties, fixes and bounds each rate for a Custom model.

Where

BiSSE Advanced fitting controls BiSSE parameter table (CSV)

Default

Empty. Click Fill parameter table for a template, and tick Custom under Models.

Change it when

You want a hypothesis the presets do not cover, such as equal extinction with state-specific speciation. Rates with the same Group are tied. See the parameter table format.

Check after

The Effective parameter constraints table in Diagnostics. Incompatible ties stop with “Tied BiSSE rates have incompatible fixed values or bounds.”





Optimizer starts
Sets how many deterministic starting points each model gets.

Where

BiSSE Advanced fitting controls

Default

3 (range 1–8)

Change it when

Starts disagree. Guane needs at least two starts to show weights.

Check after

The StartSpread column, and “BiSSE starts disagree or an unconverged attempt is better. Refit before interpreting model support.”




Verify with an independent optimizer
Refits each model with a second optimizer from its best point.

Where

BiSSE Advanced fitting controls

Default

On

Change it when

Leave it on. Without verification, Guane does not show weights.

Check after

The Verified column, and “Independent optimizer verification failed or disagreed. Weights and intervals are withheld.”

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
QuaSSE numerics


Measurement-error column
Uses a column of per-species standard errors for the continuous trait.

Where

QuaSSE Model and data settings Measurement-error column

Default

Common standard error, which uses Common measurement standard error (1)

Change it when

You have measured standard errors, in trait units. Zero and missing errors are not supported.

Check after

“The tip grid is coarser than a measurement standard error. Increase resolution; model weights are withheld.”




Trait grid bins
Sets the resolution of the trait grid that QuaSSE integrates over.

Where

QuaSSE Numerical integration controls Trait grid bins

Default

1024

Change it when

The tip grid is coarser than the measurement error, or the likelihood is unstable.

Check after

“Every fit is checked with twice the grid bins and half the time step. Unstable likelihoods suppress model weights.”

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
Worked recipe

Worked example: a custom BiSSE with tied rates
Start in the BiSSE card, with the example matched in the Data card.


Set Binary trait to habitat_binary. Observed value coded as state 0 defaults to aquatic.
Open Advanced fitting controls and click Fill parameter table.
In BiSSE parameter table (CSV), change the Group of mu1 to mu0 and the Group of q10 to q01. This ties extinction across states and makes transitions symmetric.
Under Models, tick Full, Trait-independent diversification and Custom.
Set Sampling fraction for state 0 and Sampling fraction for state 1 to 0.8 (invented values), and Optimizer starts to 5.
Click Run BiSSE. The status reads “BiSSE completed. Review convergence, bounds and model assumptions.”
Open Diagnostics and check Effective parameter constraints: the Custom model shows the tied groups.


Expect the three models to reach log-likelihoods within a few hundredths of each other, with no weights: “BiSSE ranking weights are unavailable. Inspect individual fits and diagnostics.” Diagnostics warns “A BiSSE rate reached a bound. Inspect bounds and identifiability before interpretation.” and that starts disagree for the Full model. A 19-tip tree cannot separate these models. Its transition rates run to their upper bound, the same pattern as in Advanced ancestral states. If you try Run profile uncertainty on the Full model, Guane refuses: “Resolve fit diagnostics before calculating profile intervals.”




The BiSSE parameter table with extinction and transition rates tied.


In the verification table, the Full model’s StartSpread is well above zero, while Verified and Stable are TRUE for all three models. Start disagreement alone is enough to withhold the weights.



The verification columns: only the Full model’s starts disagree.





The full BiSSE diagnostics tab for the three models.

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
When weights are withheld
Guane shows model weights only when every candidate in the run passes all of these checks:

At least two models are selected under Models.
It converged, and all of its starts converged.
Its likelihood is stable under tighter integration tolerance.
The independent optimizer verified it.
No rate sits at a bound.
Its starts agree, and there were at least two starts.
No other candidate found a better feasible point for it.
No two candidates have identical constraints.

If any check fails, the weights column stays empty. The failing check is named in Diagnostics.

title: Advanced SSE models
text:
Before you interpret






Scientific caution




A BiSSE preference for trait-dependent rates can come from rate differences unrelated to the trait. Refit in Hidden-state and null models and compare against CID-2 and CID-4.
Missing weights mean the models could not be ranked. Do not compute them yourself.
Sampling fractions and measurement errors are assumptions you supply. Report them.

Read State-dependent speciation and extinction before you report.

title: Advanced tutorials
section: How to read a control card
text:
How to read a control card
Each family page describes its controls in cards like this one:

Root probabilities (pi)
Sets the prior probability of each state at the root of a discrete reconstruction.

Where

Discrete traits Advanced analysis controls Root probabilities (pi)

Default

Equal weights

Change it when

You have independent evidence about the root state, for example from fossils or an outgroup.

Check after

Compare the root node’s probabilities with your weights. If they match exactly, the data added nothing at the root.




Where is the path to the control in the app.
Default is what Guane uses if you change nothing.
Change it when names the situation that justifies a change.
Check after tells you what to read, usually in Diagnostics, before you trust the new result.

title: Advanced tutorials
text:
Judge before you interpret
Five habits apply to every advanced control:

Read Diagnostics first. Warnings sit there, not next to the estimates.
Compare all optimizer starts. If starts reach different likelihoods, the best one may not be the global optimum.
A rate at a bound is not an estimate. It tells you the data cannot pin that rate down.
Missing weights are deliberate. Guane withholds weights and intervals when checks fail; do not rebuild them by hand.
Rerun after every change. Changing data or settings clears the affected result.

See Uncertainty and reporting, Quantities that must not be conflated and Minimum information to report.

title: Advanced tutorials
text:
Your own data
Many advanced controls take pasted tables or matrices. Custom input formats gives the exact format for each box, and Troubleshooting pasted inputs covers rejected tables.

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Before you start
Load the example in the Ancestral state reconstruction Data card and click Use matched taxa. Resolve the mismatch shows each step. The Discrete traits and Polymorphic traits cards share one collapsed section, Advanced analysis controls. It is shown unless Framework is Bayesian Mk (sample rates).

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Root and rate matrix

Root probabilities (pi)
Sets the prior probability of each state at the root.

Where

Discrete traits Advanced analysis controls Root probabilities (pi)

Default

Equal weights

Change it when

You have independent evidence about the root state, for example from fossils or an outgroup. Choose Named custom weights, click Fill equal root weights, then edit the Root weights: state,weight box. See the root weights format.

Check after

The Effective settings preview is the exact R call Guane will run. Your weights are in its pi entry, written in R’s exact hexadecimal notation: 0x1.999999999999ap-4 is 0.1, and 0x1.999999999999ap-1 is 0.8. The plain check comes after the run: the root node’s row in the node probabilities table. If the root probabilities match your weights exactly, the data added nothing at the root.




Transition rates
Chooses whether Guane estimates the rate matrix or uses one you supply.

Where

Discrete traits Advanced analysis controls Transition rates

Default

Estimate rates

Change it when

You want to reconstruct under rates taken from another study or another fit. Choose Supply fixed Q, click Fill Q template from constraints, and edit the Fixed Q: named CSV matrix box. Untick Compare with ER, SYM and ARD: a fixed Q is not fitted, so there is nothing to compare. See the fixed Q format.

Check after

“Fixed Q must preserve the selected model rate-sharing constraints.” A fixed Q has no convergence to check; its rates are your assumption.




Optimization settings
Chooses the optimizer starts and exposes the rate bounds.

Where

Discrete traits Advanced analysis controls Optimization settings

Default

Guane: three deterministic starts, with Lower rate bound (min.q) 1e-10 and Upper rate bound 100

Change it when

Starts disagree, or a rate sits at a bound and you want to test whether the bound matters. Custom starting rates opens Starting rates (q.init); see the starting rates format.

Check after

The Optimizer starts graph in Results, and in Diagnostics: “A rate is near an optimization bound. Estimates and model rankings may be unstable.” or “Starting values reached different likelihoods”.




Custom rate constraints
An index matrix that says which transitions share a rate and which are forbidden.

Where

Discrete traits Model Custom Custom rate constraints

Default

Empty; start from Start custom matrix from and click Fill custom matrix

Change it when

ER, SYM and ARD do not match your hypothesis, for example when some transitions are impossible. See the custom rate constraints format.

Check after

The Transition-rate diagram in Results shows the rates you tied and forbade. Starts and bound warnings still apply.

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Histories and posteriors

Number of histories
Sets how many stochastic character maps Guane draws. Mapping seed makes the draw repeatable.

Where

Discrete traits Framework Stochastic mapping (fixed fitted rates)

Default

100 (range 2–500), with Mapping seed 999

Change it when

Sampled frequencies disagree with the analytic node probabilities. More histories reduce Monte Carlo error.

Check after

The Monte Carlo agreement plot in Diagnostics compares sampled frequencies with analytic probabilities. A very large request stops with “Requested mapping workload is too large”.




Gamma priors and proposals (CSV)
Sets a gamma prior and a proposal variance for each rate in Bayesian Mk.

Where

Discrete traits Framework Bayesian Mk (sample rates)

Default

Empty: gamma shape 1, rate 1 and proposal variance 0.1 for every rate. Click Fill rate-prior table for a template.

Change it when

You have prior information about rates, or chains mix poorly. See the rate prior format.

Check after

The chain tables in Diagnostics. “Split-Rhat exceeds 1.01 or is unavailable. Do not treat this run as converged.”

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Continuous and polymorphic extras


Known standard-error column
Adds known measurement error to each tip.

Where

Continuous traits Use comparable marginal ML Known standard-error column

Default

None (zero error)

Change it when

Your table has a column of standard errors, on the same scale as the selected trait.

Check after

“Standard errors must be finite, nonnegative and on the selected trait scale.”




Ordered polymorphism
Allows only contiguous combinations in an order you give.

Where

Polymorphic traits Ordered polymorphism

Default

Off, with Maximum polymorphism 2

Change it when

The states have a natural order. Enter it in Constituent order (one state per line); see the constituent order format.

Check after

The Transition preview. The bundled example cannot be ordered: it has all three pairwise combinations.

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Worked recipe

Worked example: your root prior, echoed back
Start in the Discrete traits card, with the example matched in the Data card.


Set Trait for reconstruction to locomotion_3state, Framework to Maximum likelihood and Model to ER.
Open Advanced analysis controls. Set Root probabilities (pi) to Named custom weights and click Fill equal root weights.
Edit Root weights: state,weight to flying,0.1, swimming,0.1 and walking,0.8. The Effective settings preview is the exact R call Guane will run. Your weights are in its pi entry, written in R’s exact hexadecimal notation: 0x1.999999999999ap-4 is 0.1, and 0x1.999999999999ap-1 is 0.8. The plain check comes after the run: the root node’s row in the node probabilities table.
Click Run Mk reconstruction. Open Diagnostics before Results.
Set Framework to Stochastic mapping (fixed fitted rates). Set Number of histories to 200 and Mapping seed to 42, then run again.
In Diagnostics, read the Monte Carlo agreement plot.


Expect the root pie to show exactly 0.1, 0.1 and 0.8, and every other node to show one third per state. Diagnostics warns “A rate is near an optimization bound. Estimates and model rankings may be unstable.” The fitted rates sit at the Upper rate bound of 100. The stochastic maps then show very many transitions on every branch, and their node frequencies agree with the analytic probabilities.




Advanced analysis controls with custom root weights.





Sampled node frequencies agree with the analytic probabilities.








Saturated rates



The root pie is the prior you typed, not information from the data. When a rate runs to its bound, states reshuffle along every branch, and the tips say nothing about their ancestors. Under ER, three of the four discrete example traits (habitat_binary, parental_care_binary and locomotion_3state) do this: their rate stops at the Upper rate bound of 100. diet_5state stops below the bound, so check its Diagnostics yourself instead of assuming it is informative. The model comparison table may still show weights; a model at a bound does not earn its weight. Treat this pattern as a diagnostic, not a finding.

title: Advanced ancestral states
text:
Before you interpret






Scientific caution




If the root probabilities equal your prior, the data did not inform the root.
A rate at its bound is not an estimate, and weights for that model are not evidence.
A fixed Q is an assumption. Report where it came from.

Read Continuous ancestral reconstruction, Discrete and polymorphic ancestral reconstruction and Bayesian ancestral reconstruction before you report.

title: Custom input formats
text:
Skip to main content
These are the formats that Guane’s text boxes accept. Paste them into the named box in the card, not into the main trait CSV upload. Commas separate values, and each row ends with a new line. Keep exact column names and state spelling.
Before you paste:

title: Custom input formats
text:
Uploaded data files

Tree file
Upload with Load single tree in the Data card: one .nwk/.tre Newick or .nex/.nexus Nexus tree, with unique tip labels. A minimal Newick example is (Sp01:1,(Sp02:0.5,Sp03:0.5):0.5);. Method-specific requirements (rooting, positive branch lengths, ultrametricity) are checked when you run an analysis. LTT may instead accept multiple Newick tree files in its own upload control.


Trait CSV
Upload with Load traits · CSV in the Data card: one header row, one taxon per row, and a unique taxon identifier column. A small format example is:
species,body_mass,habitat_binary,resource_use_polymorphic
Sp01,12.5,forest,fruit+seed
Sp02,18.2,open,seed
Sp03,14.7,forest,fruit
Tip labels must match the taxon identifiers exactly; extra whitespace and different capitalization are different names. Continuous columns need numeric values. Count PGLM responses need nonnegative integers. Grouped-binomial PGLM needs integer successes and trials, with 0 <= successes <= trials for each taxon. A polymorphic cell joins coexisting constituent states with +, e.g. fruit+seed; it does not mean uncertainty or a missing value. The bundled 19-row trait CSV and 20-tip tree deliberately have one unmatched tip. Inspect Checking data and explicitly choose Use matched taxa before a trait analysis.

title: Custom input formats
text:
Ancestral state reconstruction

Custom rate constraints
In Discrete traits, set Model to Custom. The Custom rate constraints box appears below it, with Fill custom matrix. The Polymorphic traits card has no custom matrix box; choose one of its Model options instead.
Format: paste a square comma-separated matrix without row/column headers. Row = source state, column = destination state, both in the displayed state order. The diagonal and forbidden transitions are 0. Repeated positive integers tie rates; distinct consecutive integers 1,2,... estimate separate rates. For two displayed states, this allows different forward/backward rates:
0,1
2,0
Do not paste trait names into the matrix. The model’s allowed transitions and connectivity constraints still apply.


Root weights
In Advanced analysis controls, set Root probabilities (pi) to Named custom weights. The Root weights: state,weight box appears. The Bayesian Mk controls have a box with the same label.
Format: one state,weight row per allowed state, no header. Nonnegative finite weights with a positive total are normalized internally. For example, if the displayed states are forest and open:
forest,0.7
open,0.3


Fixed Q
In Advanced analysis controls, set Transition rates to Supply fixed Q. The Fixed Q: named CSV matrix box appears, with Fill Q template from constraints.
Format: a named numeric square CSV. The first cell of the header row can be empty; row and column names must each contain every allowed state exactly once. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative transition rates; each diagonal is minus its row’s off-diagonal sum. Rates must respect forbidden and shared transitions in the selected model. Example for forest, open:
,forest,open
forest,-0.2,0.2
open,0.1,-0.1


Starting rates
In Advanced analysis controls, set Optimization settings to Custom starting rates. Use the Starting rates (q.init) box.
Format: one numeric value, or one value per positive transition index, ordered 1,2,...; separate values with commas or spaces. Example: 0.1, 0.2. Each value must lie within the selected rate bounds. A fixed Q is not optimized, so starting rates and fitted-model comparison do not apply to it.


Bayesian Mk rate priors
Set Framework to Bayesian Mk (sample rates). Use the Gamma priors and proposals (CSV) box.
Format: exact CSV headers Parameter,Shape,Rate,ProposalVariance; one row per fitted rate index (q1, q2, etc.). All numeric values must be positive. Shape and Rate specify each gamma prior; ProposalVariance tunes the MCMC proposal. Click Fill rate-prior table to get the correct number of rows. A two-rate format example is:
Parameter,Shape,Rate,ProposalVariance
q1,1,1,0.1
q2,1,1,0.1


Bayesian BM parameters
In Continuous traits, set Framework to Bayesian BM. Use the Priors, starts and proposals (CSV) box.
Format: exact headers Parameter,Start,PriorMean,PriorVariance,ProposalVariance. Include one sig2 row followed by every internal node in the tree, using the node IDs in the filled template. The sig2 prior uses its positive PriorMean as the exponential-prior mean and must have NA in PriorVariance; node rows have normal priors with positive variance. Start and proposal variances must be valid; sig2 Start must be positive. Use Fill Bayesian parameter table rather than guessing node IDs:
Parameter,Start,PriorMean,PriorVariance,ProposalVariance
sig2,0.5,1000,NA,0.01
21,12.0,0,1000,0.01
The example above shows the format only; a real 20-tip tree requires a row for every internal node.


Constituent order
In Polymorphic traits, tick Ordered polymorphism. Use the Constituent order (one state per line) box and set Maximum polymorphism.
Format: one constituent state per line, each exactly once, in the desired order. Specify the maximum polymorphism size separately. For example:
fruit
seed
insect
Only contiguous combinations in that order are permitted. The bundled polymorphic example contains all three pairwise combinations, so no linear order of its three constituents can make every pair contiguous. Use it for unordered models. An ordered analysis needs a suitable custom dataset or an explicitly justified recoding; Guane does not silently change observed states.


State colors
In Graph controls of a discrete or polymorphic card, open Custom colors. Use the State colors: state,#RRGGBB box, or click Fill colors from palette.
Format: no-header state,#RRGGBB, with every allowed state exactly once. Example:
forest,#2277AA
open,#CC7733


Gradient colors
In Graph controls of the Continuous traits card, open Custom colors. Use the Gradient colors (hex, separated by commas) box.
Format: two to eight six-digit hex colors separated by commas or spaces, e.g. #E4F1CF, #54A37A, #0D5368. These change graphs, not estimates.

title: Custom input formats
text:
Diversification

Clade sampling fractions
In Clade-specific models, under Model and data settings, use the Clade sampling fractions (CSV) box, or click Fill sampling table.
Format: exact headers Node,Sampling; one row for each selected crown node, using the numeric IDs shown by Preview selected clades. Fractions must be in (0,1]:
Node,Sampling
24,1
31,0.8
These node IDs are illustrative; use the IDs for your tree. Selected crown clades must be eligible and non-overlapping.


Joint region sampling
In Joint clade-dependent models, under Model and data settings, use the Joint region sampling (CSV) box, or click Fill joint region tables.
Format: exact headers Region,Sampling. Include background region 0 and each chosen shift-node ID once, with fractions in (0,1]. Get the actual region IDs from Preview joint regions:
Region,Sampling
0,1
24,0.8


Custom joint constraints
In Joint clade-dependent models, under Advanced fitting controls, use the Custom joint constraints (CSV) box.
Format: exact headers Region,Lambda,Mu, one row per displayed region. In each rate cell, a nonnegative number fixes that rate or a name estimates it. Fixed Lambda must be positive. Reuse a name within the same rate type to tie regions; never reuse one name between Lambda and Mu. For example:
Region,Lambda,Mu
0,lambda_shared,0
24,lambda_shift,0


Joint parameter controls
In Joint clade-dependent models, under Advanced fitting controls, use the Joint parameter controls (CSV) box.
Format: exact headers Parameter,Start,Lower,Upper, one row per free name you want to override. Starts must be strictly inside bounds; free speciation lower bounds must be positive. For the preceding custom constraints:
Parameter,Start,Lower,Upper
lambda_shared,0.5,0.001,10
lambda_shift,0.7,0.001,10


Diversity-dependent starts
In Diversity-dependent models, under Advanced fitting controls, fields such as lambda, mu, K, r use a comma-separated numeric vector in the displayed parameter order, rather than a CSV table. The number/order of start values depends on the selected DDD model. Use the control’s displayed parameter labels and its default values as the template; keep all tolerance values positive.

title: Custom input formats
text:
SSE models

SSE parameter tables
In BiSSE, MuSSE or QuaSSE, open Advanced fitting controls. Use the BiSSE parameter table (CSV), MuSSE parameter table (CSV) or QuaSSE parameter table (CSV) box, after Fill parameter table.
Format: the shared exact headers are Parameter,Group,Fixed,Start,Lower,Upper. Parameter must match the generated template for that model. Group ties free parameters with the same name; Fixed sets a numeric value instead of estimating it. Keep a valid Group name in every row; leave Fixed blank for a free rate. For non-Custom presets, Guane replaces Group/Fixed with that preset’s constraints. The columns Start, Lower, and Upper control optimization. The available rows vary with the card, number of MuSSE states, and QuaSSE rate functions, so use Fill parameter table after choosing the model/functions and edit the result. A BiSSE format example is:
Parameter,Group,Fixed,Start,Lower,Upper
lambda0,lambda,,0.5,0,100
lambda1,lambda,,0.5,0,100
mu0,mu,0,0,0,100
mu1,mu,0,0,0,100
q01,q01,0.2,0.2,0,100
q10,q10,0.2,0.2,0,100
The Group/Fixed columns are used only by a Custom model where the card exposes one. A fixed rate must fit its bounds; check the effective constraints in Diagnostics. For QuaSSE, after changing Constant/Exponential/Sigmoid rate functions, fill the table again to refresh parameter names. Signed slopes, midpoints, and drift have different admissible ranges from positive diffusion/rate parameters.


MuSSE state table
In MuSSE, under Model and data settings, use the MuSSE state table (CSV) box, or click Fill state table.
Format: exact headers State,Sampling,RootWeight, one row per observed state. The row order defines MuSSE numeric codes 1,2,...; use the displayed mapping. Sampling is in (0,1]. Nonnegative root weights must sum to 1 when Root treatment is Given (ROOT.GIVEN). Example:
State,Sampling,RootWeight
walking,1,0.4
swimming,1,0.3
flying,1,0.3


Hidden-state custom indices
In Hidden-state and null models, open Custom model constraints. Set Hidden classes in Custom, then use Turnover indices (comma-separated), Extinction-fraction indices (comma-separated) and Transition indices (CSV, no header).
Format: choose two or four hidden classes first. The order is 0A,1A,0B,1B and, with four classes, 0C,1C,0D,1D. Turnover indices are a comma-separated vector with one positive integer per state; repeated indices tie parameters, and distinct indices must be consecutive from 1. Extinction-fraction indices have the same length but may use 0 for a fixed zero. A two-class example is turnover 1,2,3,4 and extinction fraction 1,1,1,1.
The hidden-state transition indices are a square CSV matrix without headers in that same state order. 0 forbids a transition, repeated positive integers tie transition rates, and positive indices must be consecutive. Changes in observed state and hidden class at the same step are forbidden. Click Fill custom constraints for a valid matrix, then edit only allowed cells. Do not confuse these index matrices with actual numeric Q rates. Inspect Effective parameter constraints in Diagnostics before interpreting the fit.

title: Custom input formats
text:
Troubleshooting pasted inputs
If a table is rejected, check its exact header spelling, commas, row count, duplicate names, whether you used the current tree’s node IDs and state order, and whether a model change made a filled template stale. Regenerate a template after changing states, hidden classes, rate functions or selected regions. A valid input format does not guarantee a converged model. Inspect optimization and posterior diagnostics separately. Never change data solely to make an example fit unless that recoding is scientifically justified and recorded.

title: Guane

What Guane does
It joins a phylogenetic tree to species-level traits, makes data preparation visible, fits selected models through R scientific packages, and presents figures, numerical results, diagnostics, and editable R code, through established R packages. The interface is available in English, Spanish and Portuguese.



Guane opens on the Phylo traits module with the bundled example tree loaded.

Four modules
Each module has its own Data card and its own analysis cards.


Phylo traits
Phylogenetic signal, PGLS, Pagel’s correlation and PGLM.


Ancestral state reconstruction
Continuous, discrete (Mk) and polymorphic traits.


Diversification
Lineage through time, constant-rate, time-varying, clade and diversity-dependent models.


SSE models
BiSSE, MuSSE, QuaSSE and hidden-state models.


Each module also has an advanced tutorial: Advanced phylo traits, Advanced ancestral states, Advanced diversification and Advanced SSE models.

You study evolution and want to run an analysis. Install and launch Guane, then take the interface tour.

Honest science






Scientific caution



The bundled example is synthetic. It teaches the interface; its results are not biological evidence. Before you report any result, read the scientific limitations for the method you used.

Skip to main content
After this page, you will have Guane open in your web browser. The app runs locally; the Shiny address that R prints is only reachable from your computer.

title: Install and launch
text:
Requirements

R and, optionally, RStudio.
The R packages that Guane uses. Install dependencies installs them all with one command.

title: Install and launch
text:
Get the code
Clone the repository from GitHub:
git clone https://github.com/alarconvv/Guane.git
No git? On the Guane GitHub page, choose Code, then Download ZIP, and unzip it.
Then open the Guane folder in R or RStudio. For example, open Guane.Rproj.

title: Install and launch
text:
Install dependencies
Run this once, in R, from the Guane folder:
install.packages(c("remotes", "pkgload", "devtools"))
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
This installs every package Guane uses, including optional ones that some cards need, such as hisse and DDD. It also installs Guane’s developer and test tools, so it can take 10–30 minutes. If one of those tools (for example V8) fails to install, Guane still runs.

title: Install and launch
text:
Launch
Choose the path that matches how you use Guane.

From the project folder
Run one of these in R from the project folder:
shiny::runApp(".")
or
devtools::load_all()
guane::run_app()
The first command runs the project’s app.R, which needs the pkgload package.


As an installed package
Install the package once from the project folder:
devtools::install()
Then launch it from any R session:
guane::run_app()


After launch
R prints a local address and opens the app in your browser.






Tip



To open one module only, pass its name: guane::run_app("signal"), "asr", "div" or "sse".

title: Install and launch
text:
Missing packages
If R says there is no package called 'x', run install.packages("x") and launch again. The command in Install dependencies avoids this.

title: Install and launch

Switch language
Use the language menu at the top right of the app to choose English, Español or Português. Switching language keeps your loaded data, selections and fitted results. Some backend messages and audit text stay in English.
To start in another language, pass default_lang:
guane::run_app(default_lang = "es")

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text:
Launching

R says a package is missing
Each analysis uses its own R backend. Install the package the error names, then launch Guane again. See Missing packages.


devtools:load_all() fails
Use two colons: devtools::load_all(). Then run guane::run_app(). See Launch.

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text:
Data and matching

An analysis rejects my data
Either of these messages means the tree and the trait table do not match: “Resolve data issues before running.” or “Match unique taxon labels explicitly in Data before reconstruction; at least three taxa are required.” Open Checking data in the module’s Data card and read the mismatch report. Then click Use matched taxa. Guane never prunes silently. See Resolve the mismatch.
Remember that each module has its own Data card. Loading data in Phylo traits does not load it in SSE models.


Taxon names look the same but do not match
Names must match exactly. Extra spaces and different capital letters make different names.


The trait preview shows only some rows
Trait preview shows 25 rows by default. Change Preview rows to see more. Analyses always use the whole table.

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text:
Pasted inputs

A pasted table or matrix is rejected
Check the exact header spelling, the commas, the row count and any duplicate names. Check that you used the current tree’s node IDs and state order. If you changed the model, states or regions, click the card’s fill button again to refresh the template. See Troubleshooting pasted inputs.

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text:
Results

My result disappeared
Changing data, the selected trait or model settings clears the affected result. Click the card’s run button again. Changing language or graph appearance keeps the result. See What keeps or clears a result.


An estimate, interval or model weight is missing
Guane withholds a number when it is not reliable. Common reasons are failed convergence, a rate at its bound, poor posterior mixing or incompatible likelihoods. The card’s Diagnostics tab says which check failed. An unavailable interval is not a zero-width interval. See Scientific limitations.


The node pies all look the same
With small or uninformative data, the fitted rate can run to its bound, and every node then shows near-equal probabilities. Check the bound warning in Diagnostics. See Discrete traits.

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text:
Language

Some text stays in English after I switch language
Some backend messages, audit text and code comments stay in English. Your data, selections and results do not change when you switch language. Research identifiers and observed values are never translated.

Each module has its own Data card
Every module keeps its own tree and trait table. Data you load in one module is not shared with the other three. When you switch module, load your data again in that module’s Data card.
The Data card has three columns:

Left: the Setting up panel. Load a tree and a CSV, choose the Taxon column and Numeric trait, set the Seed, and use Use matched taxa, Undo data change or Restore original inputs. Reset controls clears the Data workspace.
Centre: four tabs, Tree preview, Trait preview, Checking data and Diagnosis log. Below them, Description / Messages and Structure summarize the loaded data.
Right: controls for the open tab. With Tree preview open, this is the Graphic controls panel. With Checking data open, it holds the transformation and distribution tools.

The Data card’s Seed makes the randomization test in the Phylogenetic signal card repeatable. Cards with other random steps have their own seed control, such as MCMC seed or Simulation seed.

What to keep when reporting
